results.summary_before: This design is a simple UART transmitter that loads the text 'PSI Open IC 2026' into a shift register and clocks it out to the UART_TX pin. It uses a 100 Hz clock and has control inputs for output enable, reset, and input selection. To test, set RST_N low and provide a clock, then set RST_N high to start transmission; a UART receiver is needed to observe the output. External hardware includes a clock generator and a UART receiver. The design is a straightforward serial communication exercise.

results.summary_before: This circuit converts a 4-bit binary-coded decimal (BCD) input (0-9) to 7-segment display outputs, similar to the 7448 IC but with the modification that a zero input always turns the display off. It is implemented in Wokwi. To test, connect four switches to the inputs and a common-cathode 7-segment display to the outputs, then apply valid BCD values from 0 to 9. External hardware includes 4 switches or a DIP switch, a common-cathode 7-segment display, and 7 resistors for protection. The design provides a simple BCD-to-7-segment decoding function.

results.summary_before: This project is a controller for an Adafruit Charlieplex LED array, supporting up to 56 LEDs (7x8). It includes an SPI slave interface for loading custom display data, with each byte representing the brightness of one LED. On reset, it displays a brightness gradient across the array. Testing involves connecting the eight signal pins to the LED array and optionally using SPI to update the display. The design is notable for its efficient use of a single 8-pin bidirectional port to drive a large LED matrix and its SPI programmability.

results.summary_before: This mixed-signal project features a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) implemented as a current-starved ring oscillator, with its control voltage set by a 9-bit DAC. The VCO output drives a 5-bit counter and clock divider stages, providing divided outputs. It operates without an external clock and is tested by applying power and varying the 9-bit DAC input to observe frequency changes on the outputs, with an oscilloscope recommended for monitoring. The design demonstrates analog-digital integration using standard cells and is notable for its wide frequency range and digital controllability. Limitations include potential instability at extreme control voltages.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-bit single-cycle CPU with a simple RISC/Accumulator instruction set, containing a register file, ALU, and 7-segment decoder. Instructions and register addresses are supplied via the input pins, and results can be stored in the ALU, register file, or displayed on a 7-segment display. The design was tested using a ModelSim TCL script, and no external hardware is required. It is a compact educational CPU design that demonstrates basic processor architecture.
